byTheNumbers.title: The year in numbers
byTheNumbers.standfirst: For the first time more than half of Americans lived in towns and cities, and the country had more than nine million motor vehicles.

items.title: Population
items.summary: The 1920 census counted just over 106 million people, up 15 percent from 1910.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 1920 United States census
U.S. Census Bureau: Decennial census historical facts, 1920

items.title: A nation of towns
items.summary: The 1920 census was the first in which more than half the population lived in places classed as urban, meaning 2,500 or more residents.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 1920 United States census

items.metric: Share of the population in urban places

items.title: Motor vehicles
items.summary: Registrations reached 9.24 million, of which 8.13 million were cars and 1.11 million trucks; in 1900 the figure was 8,000.

sources.label: Historical Statistics of the United States, Table Df339-342: Motor vehicle registrations
FHWA Highway Statistics Summary to 1995, Table MV-200: Motor vehicle registrations

items.title: Telephone in the house
items.summary: More than a third of households had a telephone by the 1920s.

sources.label: UBC ETEC 540: Multi-frequency signalling (paper on the telephone, 1920)

items.title: A weekly trip to the pictures
items.summary: About 38 million tickets a week were sold in 1920, against a population of 106 million.

sources.label: Erik Lundegaard: Average weekly movie attendance for the last 100 years (citing George Lucas, Blockbusting)

byTheNumbers.scarcityNote: Life expectancy, literacy and household size could not be confirmed for 1920 from a source we opened, so they are left out.

foodAndKitchen.title: Food and the kitchen
foodAndKitchen.standfirst: Prohibition moved drinking into homes and speakeasies and brought finger food with it; ready-made foods were starting to shorten the kitchen day.

items.title: Snacks at the speakeasy
items.summary: After Prohibition began, speakeasies served bite-sized snacks such as canapés, crab cakes and deviled eggs instead of heavy meals; by 1925 tens of thousands had opened in New York City alone.

sources.label: History.com: Prohibition, speakeasies and finger foods
The Saturday Evening Post: What We Ate 100 Years Ago

items.title: The cocktail party at home
items.summary: Cocktail parties at home became fashionable and popularised finger foods: lobster canapés, caviar rolls, crabmeat cocktails, oyster toast, devilled eggs and savory cheese balls.

sources.label: History.com: Prohibition, speakeasies and finger foods

items.title: Dinner at home
items.summary: A typical home dinner of the 1920s was chicken a la king with vegetables and a salad, finished with icebox cake, devil's food cake or pineapple upside-down cake.

sources.label: The Saturday Evening Post: What We Ate 100 Years Ago

dishes: icebox cake or devil's food cake or pineapple upside-down cake

items.title: A lighter breakfast
items.summary: Breakfast shifted from heavy meat and potatoes to an egg, toast and a processed cereal such as Corn Flakes, on sale since 1898.

sources.label: The Saturday Evening Post: What We Ate 100 Years Ago

items.title: Lunch with a jellied salad
items.summary: Lunch was salads, sandwiches and soup, and creative cooks served Jell-O salads on lettuce, with celery, cabbage, cottage cheese or fruit cocktail set in the lime gelatin.

sources.label: The Saturday Evening Post: What We Ate 100 Years Ago

foodAndKitchen.scarcityNote: Most 1920s food sources describe the whole decade, not 1920. We could not find sourced 1920 grocery prices or kitchen appliance counts, so no price cards are shown.

clothingAndStyle.title: What people wore
clothingAndStyle.standfirst: Women's hair got shorter and waistlines lower; men gave up starched collars, and cheaper fabrics let ordinary women copy fashionable styles.

items.title: The bob and the cloche
items.summary: Many women wore a bob, a haircut that appeared early in the decade, and the close-fitting cloche hat suited the short styles.

sources.label: Fashion History Timeline (FIT): 1920-1929

items.title: Lower waists
items.summary: Waistlines dropped until 1923 and hemlines rose until 1926, before both turned.

sources.label: Fashion History Timeline (FIT): 1920-1929
Vogue Philippines: 1920s fashion history lesson

items.title: Jersey and artificial silk
items.summary: Jersey and artificial silk made fashionable styles cheaper, and cotton and linen were common in girls' dresses.

sources.label: Fashion History Timeline (FIT): 1920-1929

items.title: Copying fashion at home
items.summary: Simple styles could be copied at home with patterns and cheaper materials, and department stores supplied both, so fashion reached women of all means.

sources.label: Fashion History Timeline (FIT): 1920-1929

items.title: Soft collars for men
items.summary: Men's day wear moved away from starched collars and three-piece suits to soft collars and one- or two-button jackets, and sportswear became acceptable for everyday.

sources.label: Fashion History Timeline (FIT): 1920-1929

workAndWages.title: Work and wages
workAndWages.standfirst: A manufacturing week was about 48 hours, a dozen fewer than in 1900, and a year's pay had more than tripled in dollars.

items.title: A factory week
items.summary: A manufacturing worker averaged 48.1 hours a week, a railroad worker 48.0 and a coal miner 39.3.

sources.label: Historical Statistics of the United States, Table Ba4589-4591: Average weekly hours in manufacturing, 1900-1957

items.title: Average annual earnings
items.summary: Across all non-farm employees a year's earnings averaged $1,426; across all employees, farm workers included, $1,342.

sources.label: Historical Statistics of the United States, Table Ba4280-4282: Daily and annual earnings of employees, 1860-1929

workAndWages.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 1920 figures for women's work, child labour or typical household chores, so none are shown.

schoolAndChildhood.title: Growing up
schoolAndChildhood.standfirst: A pupil attended school about 121 days of a 162-day term.

items.title: The school year
items.summary: The average school term was 161.9 days, and a pupil attended 121.2 of them; three in four enrolled pupils were in school on a given day.

sources.label: NCES Digest of Education Statistics 2003, Table 36: school term and attendance, 1869-70 to 1999-2000

schoolAndChildhood.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced figures for enrolment, school costs or toys for 1920.

gettingAround.title: Getting around
gettingAround.standfirst: The car was becoming ordinary: more than nine million were registered, and the Model T alone took up to 40 percent of new car sales.

items.title: The Model T
items.summary: At its low prices the Model T at times made up as much as 40 percent of all cars sold in the United States.

sources.label: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Model T

gettingAround.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 1920 fares or journey times for streetcars, trains or intercity trips, so there are no journey cards.

keepingInTouch.title: Keeping in touch
keepingInTouch.standfirst: From November 1920 the news could come into the house by radio, though a letter still cost two cents.

items.title: The first scheduled broadcast
items.summary: KDKA in Pittsburgh began regular broadcasting on 2 November 1920 with the Harding-Cox election returns, on the air from 6 p.m. until noon the next day.

sources.label: ETHW: Milestones, Westinghouse Radio Station KDKA, 1920
U.S. Census Bureau: Decennial census historical facts, 1920

items.title: Two cents again
items.summary: The first-class letter rate, raised to 3 cents on 2 November 1917 as a temporary tax, went back to 2 cents on 30 June 1919.

sources.label: Wikipedia: War tax stamp
Mystic Stamp Company: Mail during World War I

keepingInTouch.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 1920 delivery times or telegram and long-distance telephone rates.

healthAndMedicine.title: Health and medicine
healthAndMedicine.standfirst: Pneumonia, influenza and tuberculosis still topped the list of killers, and the 1918 pandemic was a recent memory.

items.title: Influenza, pneumonia and tuberculosis
items.summary: Influenza and pneumonia together killed 207.3 people per 100,000 and tuberculosis 113.1 in 1920, according to a table of Public Health Service series.

sources.label: VCU: Death rates by cause of death, 1900-2001

sensitivity.note: This item describes deaths from disease.

healthAndMedicine.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced doctor fees, hospital costs or vaccination figures for 1920.

leisureAndFun.title: Evenings, weekends and festivals
leisureAndFun.standfirst: Prohibition made the speakeasy a new kind of evening out, and the cinema drew about a third of the population every week.

items.title: Drinking underground
items.summary: Prohibition drove drinking into illegal speakeasies in small towns and cities, from drab basements to upscale restaurants such as the 21 Club.

sources.label: History.com: Prohibition, speakeasies and finger foods

leisureAndFun.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced material for sport, holidays or music in 1920.

spotlight.title: Prohibition and the vote for women
spotlight.standfirst: Within a year two amendments changed everyday life: one closed the bars, the other opened the polling place to women.

items.title: Prohibition takes effect
items.summary: The Eighteenth Amendment was ratified on 16 January 1919 when Nebraska became the 36th state, and took effect on 17 January 1920.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Eighteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution
Smithsonian Institution: 1920, a year in the collections

items.title: The Volstead Act
items.summary: Congress passed the Volstead Act on 28 October 1919, overriding President Wilson's veto; it defined an intoxicating drink as one with 0.5 percent alcohol or more.

sources.label: TribLive: Timeline of events important to Prohibition
History.com: Prohibition, speakeasies and finger foods

items.title: The vote for women
items.summary: The Nineteenth Amendment was ratified on 18 August 1920 when Tennessee became the 36th state, and proclaimed by the Secretary of State on 26 August.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution
National Archives: Constitutional Amendments series, Amendment XIX

items.title: Women voters before 1920
items.summary: Fifteen states had given women equal voting rights by 1918, so the amendment extended to the rest of the country a right many women already held.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

items.title: The first national vote with women
items.summary: The presidential election of 2 November 1920 was the first in which women could vote in all 48 states; the popular vote rose from 18.5 million in 1916 to 26.8 million.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 1920 United States presidential election
